Prozo ships releases almost every alternate day across ProShip, Control Tower, ProWMS, and ProOMS, powered by AI-first development workflows using Claude and other AI platforms. In this environment, the traditional QA role has fundamentally changed. You will not operate in isolation writing test cases from a spec document. Instead, you will be embedded with both business teams and engineering teams from the very start of the product requirement stage, understanding what is being built, why it matters operationally, and what "correct" looks like in a live supply chain. Your primary focus will be ProShip, Prozo's multi-modal freight management platform that powers D2C parcel delivery across 30+ courier partners and 25,900+ pin codes. You will also support Control Tower, ProWMS, and ProOMS on a need basis. This role is based at the Panchkula office because the core ProShip business and operations team sits here, giving you direct, daily access to the people who define what the product must do. We are looking for a curious, fast learner who wants to build a career in quality engineering at a company where technology moves fast and the learning curve is steep. KEY RESPONSIBILITY AREAS 1. Manual Test Design & Execution (ProShip - Primary) Design and execute manual test cases for ProShip features: courier allocation (PACE engine), shipment creation, label generation, NDR/NPR workflows, COD management, RTO processing, weight reconciliation, pricing logic, zone mapping, and pickup scheduling. Validate end-to-end order flows across ProShip: from order ingestion through manifest generation, courier assignment, tracking updates, delivery confirmation, and returns processing. Ensure every release meets functional and business-logic requirements before it reaches production. Test API integrations between ProShip and external systems: marketplace connectors, courier partner APIs, brand OMS/ERP integrations, and webhook/callback mechanisms. Verify data accuracy across system boundaries. Perform regression testing after every release cycle to ensure new features do not break existing functionality. Given the alternate-day release cadence, regression discipline is critical. 2. Cross-Platform QA Support (Control Tower, ProWMS, ProOMS) Provide manual testing support for Control Tower modules on a need basis: SLA dashboards, escalation management, CT Score, CCTV/PSG module, billing automation, and operational analytics. Support ProWMS and ProOMS testing when required: inbound processing, inventory governance, pick-pack-ship workflows, cycle count, order orchestration, marketplace sync, and inventory allocation across channels. 3. Business-Integrated Testing & Collaboration Participate in product requirement discussions and technical requirement reviews alongside business and engineering teams. Understand the "why" behind every feature so your testing catches business-logic gaps, not just UI bugs. Work closely with the ProShip business team (co-located in Panchkula) to understand real-world freight operations: how brands use the platform, what errors impact shipments, and which edge cases occur in live operations. Translate this operational knowledge into smarter test scenarios. Collaborate with developers and the QA Lead (Noida) through daily standups, sprint planning, and release sign-off calls. Prozo's technology team is distributed across locations; you should be comfortable communicating clearly in writing and working asynchronously. 4. Defect Management & Process Improvement Log defects with clear reproducibility details: steps to reproduce, expected vs. actual behaviour, environment, screenshots/recordings, and severity classification. Well-documented bugs get fixed faster. Track defect trends, identify recurring issue patterns, and flag systemic root causes to the engineering team. Maintain and keep the test case repository current as features evolve with every release. 5. Automation Readiness & AI-First QA Practices Use AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, and similar) to accelerate test case generation, exploratory testing, and test data preparation. Prozo operates AI-first; you will be encouraged and trained to use AI to multiply your productivity from day one. Build foundational skills in test automation tools (Selenium, Cypress, Postman, or equivalent) over time. While this role is primarily manual testing, you will progressively take on semi-automated and automated testing responsibilities as you grow. QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE Minimum 3 year of hands-on experience in manual software testing/ Automation testing or QA. We are not considering freshers for this role. If you have frontend, backend, or any other tech-related experience and want to transition into QA, we are happy to evaluate your profile as well. Familiarity with software development lifecycles and Agile/Scrum methodology. You should understand how QA fits into sprint-based delivery. Prior experience in logistics, e-commerce, SaaS, or supply chain technology is a plus but not required. Willingness to adopt an AI-first working style. You do not need to be an AI expert today, but you should be curious, open to learning, and excited about using AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT to make your testing faster and more thorough. This is non-negotiable. Experience with API testing (Postman or equivalent), browser developer tools, basic SQL for database validation, and test management tools (Jira, TestRail, or similar). If you do not have these today, you should be eager to learn them quickly. Strong analytical thinking and attention to detail. You should be able to look at a feature, think about what could go wrong, and design test scenarios that cover those edge cases. Good written and verbal communication skills. You will document bugs, write test plans, and participate in cross-location standups with both business and technical teams. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field from a reputable institution. WORKING AT PROZO Work from Office:This is an in-office role, co-located with the ProShip business team. Monday to Saturday, with alternate Saturdays off (2nd and 4th Saturday). Standard business hours with flexibility required during release windows and critical deployment cycles. Distributed technology team. You will collaborate with developers across Noida, Gurugram, and Panchkula. collaboration tools (Slack, Google Meet, Jira) is essential. Fast-paced, AI-native engineering culture. Prozo uses Claude and AI-first development workflows across the stack. About Prozo Prozo is India's integrated supply chain operating system, a technology-led 3PL/4PL platform operating 50+ fulfilment centres across 3M+ sq ft, serving 120+ enterprise brands including Tira (Reliance), Pepe Jeans, Bata, Philips, Daikin, Snitch, bewakoof, and others. title: Embedded Networking Engineer - Layer 2/Layer 3
description:
We build and extend firmware for managed industrial Ethernet switches used in factories, utilities, transportation and other environments where the network cannot go down. You will work on the protocol stack at the heart of these switches: how frames are bridged, how loops are prevented, how a ring recovers within milliseconds when a link fails, and how traffic is routed between networks. The role suits a hands-on engineer who has shipped Layer 2 and Layer 3 features on real switch hardware, knows the standards well enough, and can trace a convergence problem from a packet capture down to the switch ASIC. Redundancy work and recovery-time optimization is a core part of the current work. 
 
 Responsibilities 
 Design, implement and maintain Layer 2 features on embedded switch platforms: VLANs, MAC learning and ageing, link aggregation (LACP), LLDP, IGMP/MLD snooping, port security and QoS. Own spanning-tree and redundancy features: STP, RSTP and MSTP, Distributed RSTP (DRSTP) and ring coupling, including analyzing and optimizing failover and recovery times. Design, implement and maintain Layer 3 features: static and dynamic routing (OSPF, RIP), ARP and neighbor discovery, VRRP, DHCP relay, IPv4 and IPv6 forwarding, and VRF where the platform supports it. Work across the control plane and data plane: integrate protocol software with the switch silicon through the vendor SDK (Broadcom, Marvell or similar), covering table programming, port and trunk configuration, CPU packet path, hardware events and link-state handling. Debug complex field and lab issues across the stack using packet captures, traffic generators, SDK diagnostics and kernel or system logs; drive root-cause analysis to closure. Write design documents and test plans; review code and designs from other engineers. Work with test teams on protocol conformance, interoperability and performance testing, including convergence-time measurement. Interact directly with customers on technical requirements, feasibility studies and issue resolution. 
 
 Required experience and skills 
 Hands-on Layer 2 and Layer 3 protocol know-how is mandatory for this role. 
 
 Experience 
 5-6 years of software development on Layer 2 and Layer 3 networking, on embedded switch or router platforms. A track record of shipping protocol features into production, not only maintaining them. 
 
 Layer 2 (mandatory) 
 Strong working knowledge of IEEE 802.1D, 802.1w (RSTP), 802.1s (MSTP), 802.1Q and 802.1AX (LACP), including state machines, timers and edge cases. Experience with LLDP, IGMP/MLD snooping, MAC table management and Layer 2 QoS. 
 
 Layer 3 (mandatory) 
 Solid knowledge of IPv4 and IPv6 forwarding, ARP and neighbor discovery, static routing and at least one dynamic routing protocol (OSPF preferred). Experience with VRRP and DHCP relay. 
 
 Control plane and data plane 
 Clear understanding of control plane, data plane and management plane separation on switches and routers, and how protocol state is programmed into hardware forwarding tables. Experience on the control plane: protocol state machines, the CPU packet path (trapping, punting and injecting control frames such as BPDUs, LACPDUs and routing packets), and control-plane policing. Experience on the data plane: programming MAC, VLAN, L3 host and route tables, ACLs and QoS in the ASIC, and handling hardware events such as link changes, table-full and learning events. Ability to debug mismatches between software state and hardware state, and to optimize the path from a control-plane decision to the data plane, which is critical for fast convergence. 
 
 Embedded and platform 
 Expert C programming in a multi-threaded embedded environment; working knowledge of C++ and scripting (Python or shell). Embedded Linux: cross-compilation, build systems, kernel/user-space interaction, IPC and debugging with gdb and tracing tools. Experience with a switch ASIC SDK (Broadcom, Marvell or similar). Fluent with Wireshark, traffic generators (Ixia, Spirent or similar) and lab test setups. 
 
 Preferred 
 Hands-on experience with Distributed DRSTP or comparable redundancy schemes (for example multi-chassis link aggregation, IEEE 802.1AX DRNI, MRP/IEC 62439-2 or ERPS/G.8032), including tuning for fast recovery. Experience with industrial Ethernet switch platforms, for example Hirschmann HiOS, Moxa, Siemens SCALANCE or Cisco Industrial Ethernet. Familiarity with industrial redundancy and timing standards: IEC 62439 (MRP, HSR/PRP), IEEE 1588 PTP. Exposure to secure development practices, ideally IEC 62443-4-1/4-2. Management-plane work: CLI, SNMP/MIB design, web management, NETCONF/YANG. Experience connecting devices to cloud management platforms (TLS, MQTT, NATS or WebSockets). Prior customer-facing role in feasibility studies or effort estimation. 
 
 Education 
 Bachelors or Masters degree in Electronics, Electrical, Computer Science, Telecommunications or a related field, or equivalent experience.
